# DMA26: differentiated author disposition after the existing source applications

**Recommendation: retain the 206 positive-consideration proposal and recommend these exact 26 for independent researched-unresolved consideration, for the eleven specific reasons below.** None is automatically accepted as unresolved. This is an authored scientific recommendation, not an independent review, a new supported partition, a physical reclassification or an adopted decision. The sole 232-key native/authority qualification remains successful and unchanged.

The same proposed outcome for 26 does not derive from the number or the invalid USCB outside flag. The additional deciding work here was a close reading of each flagged center's already-saved CHARIM position, with the unmarked source panel, previously plotted original source lines and actual source-method evidence. Some placements visibly disagree with the mapped land portrayal; others are too close to combined road/coast symbols for that map to decide. The latter are not asserted to be offshore. Both kinds leave an actual source-application question after reasonable use of the available bodies. No queried geometry was repaired and no predicate, fit, transformation, physical/native/authority run, source producer or new plot was performed.

## What remains positive, and what failed to resolve

All 26 retain the original recorded single-parish/aggregate-owner support and land support, without a recorded inland-water hit. These original witnesses are not new vector-center containment claims. All ten whole parish geometries, selected aggregate owner 7115, original complete-source physical evidence and the sole technical qualification of 232 remain. Whole-member reconstruction issues are not attributed to these cells by parish name. Administrative membership of each parish in Dominica is not in dispute. A difference between internal parishes aggregated to the same country is not a competing national owner.

The failed additional qualification is **source-level discrimination of the exterior portrayal at these exact settings**, not failure of the stock predicate. The original source is a Commons-derived parish map with the retained 2005 representation / 2022 construction lineage. The actually read CHARIM topographic map (April 2016, 1:50,000) supplies declared WGS84/UTM20N display controls and useful occupied-land, coast, mouth and road portrayals. Its imagery/DEM method statements do not establish a coastline survey date, tidal convention or a measured coastline error. The saved coordinate application makes the map genuinely usable; it does not make thin shoreline symbols a precise boundary test.

The actual USCB national source is a census-attribute mapping product derived from HDX input accessed 11 May 2021. The 2011 census label and 2021 processing dates are not coast survey dates. The accompanying note expressly disclaims a guarantee of boundary-placement accuracy. Its parish adjustment for settlements does not prove a national coastline correction, and the ten parishes are not automatically equated to the single national feature. More articulated lines and later processing do not establish superiority. The original national ring is invalid; its reported self-intersection and repeated vertices remain untouched. Conditional outside results are not reliable membership certificates, distances in degrees are not uncertainty tolerances, and separation from the documented defect does not validate the rest of the polygon.

Nonetheless, the already plotted original outlines show real local line-placement differences, and CHARIM provides actual corroborative or inconclusive coastal context. Dismissing all of that because one ring is invalid would discard material evidence. Conversely, treating its outside flags as a veto would overstate it. My recommendation rests on the remaining ambiguity after the map application and method comparison, weighed against—not replacing—the original positive witnesses.

## Exact contextual dispositions

The companion JSON retains all 26 original comparison/witness rows unchanged, the exact keys, eleven group rationales and existing map locators. Panel coordinates are simple indexing into the retained display/crop records; they are not a new map fit. Visual descriptions below are qualitative source readings, not pixel segmentation or geographic predicates.

### john-north2: Clifton and Toucari/Tanetane west coast

Exact keys: [7115,119561,86321], [7115,119576,86322].

Saved panel positions (299.60,290.72) and (318.09,539.41) sit against the narrow western coastal outline; the latter is visibly on the blue side near the road/shore bend. The map establishes occupied mainland nearby, not a clear interior placement for these two centers.

The original parish/land support remains affirmative, but settlement presence cannot decide these edge positions. The separate conditional national-line discrepancy is material in this setting. The declared-control map application did not resolve which exterior portrayal should control. **Recommendation: researched-unresolved consideration.**

### john-headland1: Southern edge of headland west of Stowe/Grange

Exact keys: [7115,119591,86322].

Saved panel position (319.89,788.25) is at the southern edge/blue side of the headland-neck depiction. The existing original-vector plot separately shows the USCB exterior north of this center and a different frozen-source line nearby.

Correct the broad favorable-context inference for this singleton: the other 44 headland records do not establish this edge. This is not a newly disproved national affiliation, but a failed exact-edge corroboration after actual map and original-line reading. Preserve its historical membership in favorable76. **Recommendation: researched-unresolved consideration.**

### andrew-bay1: Batibou / Anse-de-Mai embayment

Exact keys: [7115,119583,86382].

Saved panel position (140.78,141.13) is on the blue side of the small embayment next to a coastal projection and road; the adjacent eastern marker is a different key.

Nearby road and land projections explain the positive source-support context but cannot transfer an interior interpretation to the western center. The detailed map does not resolve the original exterior disagreement in favor of the frozen representation. **Recommendation: researched-unresolved consideration.**

### peter-coast2: Bioche and southern Colihaut coastal bends

Exact keys: [7115,119652,86319], [7115,119676,86326].

Saved positions (243.06,504.79) and (362.85,902.30) are at the seaward coast/road bends. The source-only panel confirms that the white road and black coastal outline are adjacent, rather than an independently controlled land-width measurement.

These are small coastal projections/road-edge contexts, not disagreement about parish identity. The map supports nearby land occupation but the attempted source application leaves these exact exterior placements unresolved. No road-buffer or symbol-width tolerance is inferred. **Recommendation: researched-unresolved consideration.**

### joseph-town3: St Joseph coastal frontage

Exact keys: [7115,119725,86349], [7115,119726,86349], [7115,119727,86349].

Saved x approximately243, y422/439/455 places the three markers west of the depicted coastal town frontage. The original-source plot shows an articulated USCB line east of the straighter frozen segment in this neighborhood.

Here the adverse evidence is the combined readable coastal portrayal and actual original-line difference, not the conditional query alone. The retained positive source/land support and technical pass do not remove the unresolved exterior-source applicability. **Recommendation: researched-unresolved consideration.**

### joseph-layou1: Layou river-mouth / coastal shoulder

Exact keys: [7115,119733,86350].

Saved position (260.76,554.72) is on the west coastal shoulder beside the depicted Layou outlet and settlement. Channel, mouth and coast are separately visible; no channel is promoted to an administrative exclusion.

The failed qualification is choosing the exterior portrayal at this source-sensitive mouth/shore setting. The original absence of inland-water support is retained; neither this map symbol nor the USCB point result reclassifies the cell. **Recommendation: researched-unresolved consideration.**

### paul-road2: Canefield / River Estate waterfront

Exact keys: [7115,119784,86372], [7115,119785,86372].

Saved positions (244.75,621.01) and (244.87,637.62) coincide with or lie on the blue side of the narrow western coastal-road depiction. The source-only panel does not yield an unambiguous interior margin.

Substantial built-up land immediately east is positive contextual evidence, but does not decide these two coastal-edge positions. The original USCB placement is only auxiliary and invalidity-limited; the controlled map reading itself also fails to settle the edge. **Recommendation: researched-unresolved consideration.**

### george-waterfront1: Newtown waterfront south of Roseau

Exact keys: [7115,119812,86383].

Saved position (224.14,206.79) is on the blue side of the road/coast depiction at Newtown. The urban context is certain at map scale, while this marker is not clearly interior to it.

Do not infer exact territorial extent from the city name or built-up symbols. The positive source/physical witness and completed qualification remain, but this source application leaves a concrete unresolved exterior representation question. **Recommendation: researched-unresolved consideration.**

### luke-coast8: Pointe Michel northern frontage, southern town edge and coastal slope

Exact keys: [7115,119830,86386], [7115,119831,86386], [7115,119839,86386], [7115,119840,86386], [7115,119844,86387], [7115,119846,86388], [7115,119847,86388], [7115,119848,86388].

The saved positions separate two northern coast-edge markers, two at the southern town edge, one on the following slope edge and three farther south. Several are visibly blue-side; the northern pair is closer to the drawn coastline. The original-line plot shows the straight frozen segments versus more articulated USCB exterior in all these neighborhoods.

These eight are not evidence that the whole24 Pointe Michel context fails. They are the exact local line-sensitive subset for which retained map reading and original-source comparison failed to resolve the exterior application. Road/slope/settlement evidence is preserved without extending it across the shoreline. **Recommendation: researched-unresolved consideration.**

### patrick-coast2: Fond St Jean / Bagatelle coastal-road bends

Exact keys: [7115,119848,86455], [7115,119849,86451].

Saved positions (273.88,140.72) and (207.10,157.87) meet the coast/white-road depiction and its southern bend. This is less decisive visual adversity than the clearly blue-side St Joseph frontage: fine land, road and shoreline symbols meet here.

These two cannot be rejected by the small conditional angular offset or cleared by a road symbol. The actual map application is inconclusive at the deciding edge, while a second original exterior differs. Recommend unresolved consideration for the failed discrimination, not because USCB is presumed superior or a new accuracy certificate is universally required. **Recommendation: researched-unresolved consideration.**

### mark-connection3: Northern-facing Scotts Head connection

Exact keys: [7115,119871,86390], [7115,119871,86391], [7115,119871,86392].

Saved x157.53/174.26/190.99 at y approximately141 lies along the blue side/northern edge of the connected Scotts Head neck. The source-only map confirms connected land south of these markers; the original-line plot exposes the different northern-facing outline.

The map resolves the broad island-versus-connected-promontory question positively, but not these three exact northern-edge placements. That useful institutional/physical context is retained; it does not automatically clear the source-sensitive edge. No islet sovereignty question is manufactured. **Recommendation: researched-unresolved consideration.**

## Material distinctions and the preserved historical correction

The Saint Joseph frontage and several Pointe Michel/Scotts Head positions supply visually adverse water-side placements. Fond St Jean and some coastal-road bends instead leave an unresolved thin-symbol interpretation. These are different evidentiary strengths; neither becomes a surveyed exclusion. The Scotts Head reading affirmatively resolves its broad connected-promontory setting, while failing to resolve the three northern-edge positions. Layou is treated as a river-mouth/coast question without converting a channel symbol into an administrative veto. The urban and road settings retain positive evidence of nearby occupied land without extending it across a line.

The particularly consequential correction is **[7115,119591,86322]**. It remains in the historical favorable76. The earlier broad headland interpretation is insufficient at this southern edge, where the retained display and original-line plot reveal the local difference. No conclusion is transferred from the other 44 headland keys. This recommendation preserves the original 76/156 record, now transparently relating this subset to one former favorable and 25 former mixed cells. It does not rewrite the prior artifact or imply the other 156 were adverse.

The cumulative authored proposal is therefore 206 positive consideration (75 former favorable + 131 former mixed), plus 26 researched-unresolved consideration (1 + 25), all still requiring independent scientific acceptance. It is not a declaration of 206 accepted or 26 accepted-unresolved cells. The separately preserved 174 original nonland-context records remain outside the suspended232 claim and unadjudicated. No ownership, source, class, native result or authority membership has changed.

## Finite source queue and exact remaining gate

The held CHARIM page, controls/credits and relevant neighborhood panels have been read, and the newly readable USCB catalogue, attached active method records, original national geometry and conditional application have now also been read. These actual attempts produced the bounded ambiguity described above. Repeating the native run, original query or map fit cannot answer it. An arbitrary repair of the invalid ring would manufacture a new reference. A different USCB parish/settlement layer is not established as an independent shoreline survey or a deciding national-exterior source merely because it is available in the same FileGDB; no unperformed predicate on those layers is claimed necessary or completed.

The specifically identified CDEMA national service remains stopped after certificate-verification failure; the World Bank catalogue's later local materialization remains stopped at HTTP403 (its earlier web reading is preserved). Neither is declared absent or scientifically exhausted. They remain possible future evidence only if a genuinely changed lawful access situation supplies actual content. No currently identified, accessible, unread deciding primary passage or controlled coast layer has been left idle in this bounded queue. This is a finite source-relative recommendation, not a demand to obtain a universal sovereignty certificate, a new coast survey, or every conceivable publication.

The remaining immediate gate is the parent's separate independent review of these reasons and exact evidence. The reviewer can accept or reject this authored unresolved proposal under the actual contract; it is not predetermined by the auxiliary query. If the reviewer instead accepts some original source-relative positives, that should explain why the actual local alternative portrayals do not materially defeat those particular assignments. No new technical failure, synthetic exception or award is asserted here.

## Existing public and review custody

The unchanged technical/source handoff is public at d33a5690dc5db1b7e3d2c1258da9c07680731481, with the dated USCB research update at **5c22fac153e35b2a7c314a160e7b264ba3ab7b3f**, in `data/regional-review/dma232-whole10-physical-20261025/source-review-update-20261025/`. Those bodies are not rewritten by this addendum.

The actual source-reading/control/figure custody remains Library **libfile_0b129a6f1df88191a2169ad28d28385b, version0**, file `file_00000000619081f6a86aeff2f633eb36`, `DMA232-source-review-supplement-20261025.zip`, 2,960,958 bytes, SHA256 `3082f32bb0a8022bf398cbc05b597af8d5ac236e2cf451e3dbc9481cf41b1cf8`. It holds the original26 comparison, saved232 display positions, nine relevant CHARIM excerpts, actual USCB method and source-line figure. This new author addendum replaces only the earlier unspecified judgment request for26; no full bundle or raw archive is duplicated here.

This packet is local author evidence for the coordinator. No new Library upload, Git change/push, PR, dispatch, integration or acceptance occurred in this continuation. Ordinary evidence in any arbitrary format remains authorized through supported access, actual restrictions remain in force, and any later repository publication must use normal owned-worktree Git push only.
